en: Parivāra 8.
Questions and Answers on the Uposatha and Other Matters: 1.
Questions Concerning the Beginning, Middle, and End.
What is the beginning of the Uposatha procedure, what is its middle, and what is its conclusion?
What is the beginning of the Pavāraṇā procedure, what is its middle, and what is its conclusion?
What is the beginning of the Tajjanīya procedure, what is its middle, and what is its conclusion?
Of the act of censure … [and so on] … of the act of banishment … [and so on] … of the act of reconciliation … [and so on] …
...of the act of suspension (*ukkhepanīyakamma*) ...
of the granting of probation (*parivāsa*) ...
of sending back to the beginning (*mūlāyapaṭikassanā*) ... [and so on] ...

What is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the end of the act of granting the *mānatta* penance... [and so on] ...of the act of rehabilitation (*abbhāna*)... [and so on] ...of the act of full ordination (*upasampadā*)?

2. Exposition of the Beginning, Middle, and End.
What is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the end of the Uposatha procedure?
The beginning of the Uposatha procedure is the assembly; the middle is the performance; the end is the conclusion.
What is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the end of the *pavāraṇā* procedure?
The beginning of the *pavāraṇā* procedure is concord; the middle is the performance; the end is the conclusion.
What is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the end of the *tajjanīya* (reprimand) procedure?

For a formal act of censure (*tajjanīya-kamma*), the subject matter and the person involved constitute the beginning; the motion (*ñatti*) is the middle; and the proclamation of the formal act (*kammavācā*) is the conclusion.
For a formal act of demotion (*niyassakamma*) … [and so on] … for a formal act of banishment (*pabbājanīyakamma*) … [and so on].
...of the act of reconciliation (paṭisāraṇīyakamma) ...
of the act of suspension (ukkhepanīyakamma) ...
of the granting of probation (parivāsa) ... [and so forth] ...

What is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the end of the sending back to the beginning (*mūlāya-paṭikassanā*), of the granting of the period of penance (*mānatta-dāna*), and of the rehabilitation (*abbhāna*)?
The subject matter and the person are the beginning of the procedure for rehabilitation (*abbhāna*); the motion (*ñatti*) is the middle; the formal proclamation (*kammavācā*) is the conclusion.
What is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the conclusion of the ordination procedure (*upasampadā-kamma*)?
The person is the beginning of the ordination procedure; the motion is the middle; the formal proclamation is the conclusion.
What is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the end of the lifting of a *tajjanīya-kamma* (act of censure)?
The proper conduct (*sammāvattanā*) is the beginning of the lifting of a *tajjanīya-kamma*, the motion (*ñatti*) is the middle, and the formal act (*kammavācā*) is the end.
[The same applies to] the *niyassakamma* (act of subordination)…pe…
What is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the end of the lifting of a formal act of banishment …pe… of a formal act of reconciliation …pe… and of a formal act of suspension?
For the rescinding of the act of suspension (*ukkhepanīyakamma*), right conduct is the beginning, the motion (*ñatti*) is the middle, and the formal proclamation (*kammavācā*) is the conclusion.
As for the verdict of mindfulness (*sativinaya*): what is its beginning, what is its middle, and what is its conclusion?
For the verdict of mindfulness, the matter and the person are the beginning, the motion is the middle, and the formal proclamation is the conclusion.
Of the verdict for one who is no longer confused … [and so on] … of the verdict of further penalty … [and so on] … of the covering over as with grass … [and so on] …
...by the authorization as an instructor of bhikkhunīs ...
by the authorization for not being separated from the three robes ...
by the authorization for a rug ... etc.
...by the authorization for the discarder of silver ...
by the authorization for the receiver of the upper garment ...
by the authorization for the receiver of the alms-bowl ... etc.
Regarding the authorization for a staff …pe… the authorization for a carrying-net …pe… the authorization for both a staff and a carrying-net:
what is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the conclusion?
The matter and the person are the beginning of the formal authorization for the staff and the sling; the motion is the middle; the formal act (kammavācā) is the conclusion.
The answering of questions regarding the Uposatha and other matters is finished.
